sources.source_role_and_hypotheses: Theorem 1.1: a universal C>0 gives at most exp(exp(exp(epsilon^(-C)))) origin rotations of the open stripe for every 0<epsilon<1/10; the same family covers closed stripes. Page 2 explicitly records 1/(2epsilon). The authored lower bound improves this cited baseline by asymptotic factor pi, not by order. Section 8.2 allows dilation and is a different problem. The upper-bound proof was not fully audited or reproduced; no exponent improvement is claimed.

sources.title: Rotations by roots of unity and Diophantine approximation

recorded_audit_page_inspections.scope: Theorem 1.1 uncovered-point thresholds and closed-strip Problem 1.2

sources.source_role_and_hypotheses: Theorem 1.1: for root order n>1, all fractional parts of Re(X omega^k) can lie in (epsilon,1-epsilon) exactly for epsilon<(p-1)/(2p), where p is the smallest odd prime divisor of n, or epsilon<1/2 when n is a power of two. Thus equally spaced unoriented directions fail for epsilon<1/3 by applying the theorem to 2m-th roots; opposite normals define the same strip and a global rotation is absorbed into X. This is credited, not new, and its full proof was not independently re-proved.
